description: Programming with functions as values: the lambda calculus, pure functions, folds, algebraic data types, laziness, type inference and monads. Students write functional programs in the code runner, using Python and JavaScript in a strict functional style, and step through evaluation and call stacks in the visualiser.
modelledOn: Abelson and Sussman, Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
Bird and Wadler, Introduction to Functional Programming
outcomes: Reduce lambda-calculus terms by hand and encode booleans, numbers and recursion with Church encodings and fixed points.
Write programs from pure functions, higher-order functions and folds without mutating state.
Model data with algebraic data types and process it by exhaustive pattern matching and structural recursion.
Convert recursive definitions to tail-recursive form and explain stack use, memoisation and lazy evaluation.
Infer principal types for small programs and use parametric polymorphism, functors and monoids.
Structure effects with Maybe, Either, State and Writer monads and keep side effects at the edge of a program.

units.title: The lambda calculus
topics: Lambda terms: abstraction, application, free and bound variables, alpha conversion
Beta reduction, normal forms, normal-order versus applicative-order evaluation, and the Church-Rosser theorem
Church encodings of booleans, pairs and natural numbers; arithmetic by function application
Recursion without names: fixed points and the Y combinator

units.title: Purity and immutability
topics: Pure functions and referential transparency; equational reasoning
Side effects and why they complicate testing, caching and concurrency
Immutable data and persistent structures with structural sharing
Substitution model versus environment model of evaluation
Proving properties of functions by equation and induction, such as map fusion

units.title: Higher-order functions and folds
topics: First-class functions, closures and lexical scope
map, filter and zip as the vocabulary of list processing
foldr and foldl: definitions, differences and expressing sum, length and reverse as folds
Currying, partial application and function composition
Pipelines, point-free style and list comprehensions

units.title: Algebraic data types and pattern matching
topics: Product types and sum types; tagged unions in Python and JavaScript
Pattern matching and exhaustiveness checking
Recursive types: lists, binary trees and expression trees
Option and Either types replacing null and exceptions
Structural recursion and folds over trees (catamorphisms)

units.title: Recursion and tail calls
topics: Structural recursion and its correspondence with induction
Accumulators, tail recursion and tail-call elimination
Mutual recursion and trampolines to avoid stack overflow
Cost of recursion: stack depth, repeated work in naive Fibonacci and memoisation
Divide and conquer in functional style: merge sort and quicksort on immutable lists

units.title: Lazy evaluation and infinite structures
topics: Call-by-value, call-by-name and call-by-need; thunks and sharing
Infinite lists and streams: naturals, Fibonacci numbers and the sieve of Eratosthenes with generators
Laziness and control: short-circuit operators and user-defined control structures
Space leaks, strictness and when laziness costs memory
Lazy dynamic programming and memoisation through lazy tables

units.title: Types, inference and polymorphism
topics: Parametric polymorphism: type variables, generic functions and free theorems
Hindley-Milner type inference: constraint generation and unification
Ad-hoc polymorphism: type classes, interfaces and overloading
Functors: mapping over containers and the functor laws
Monoids, semigroups and folding with associativity: parallel reduction

units.title: Monads, effects and project
topics: Applicative functors: combining independent effectful computations
The monad interface: bind, return and the monad laws
Maybe, Either, List, State and Writer monads worked through examples
Effects at the edge: functional core with an imperative shell, and input and output
Project: a parser-combinator library and an interpreter for a small expression language

schedule.title: The lambda calculus
schedule.exercise: Reduce five lambda terms to normal form by hand, writing each beta step, then encode the number 3 and compute 2 + 3 with Church numerals.

tasks.title: Step through the reduction of five small lambda terms, marking each variable as free or bound and noting where alpha conversion avoids a capture
Implement Church booleans, pairs and numerals as functions in JavaScript, then compute successor, addition and multiplication and decode results back to integers
Write the Y combinator in a strict language using the delayed variant, define factorial through it, and explain why the plain Y loops forever

schedule.title: Purity and equational reasoning
schedule.exercise: Rewrite an impure function that uses a global counter into a pure one, then prove by induction that map f (map g xs) equals map (f after g) xs.

tasks.title: Classify ten small functions as pure or impure, rewrite the impure ones to take and return state, and show a test that now needs no setup
Implement an immutable stack and an immutable binary tree with structural sharing, and check that old versions stay unchanged after ten updates
Trace the same program under the substitution model and the environment model in the visualiser and identify one program where they give different explanations

schedule.title: Closures, map, filter and fold
schedule.exercise: Write sum, product, length, reverse and a function that groups marks into grade bands, each as a fold, and say whether foldl or foldr suits each.

tasks.title: Use map, filter and zip, with no loops, to compute the average of passing marks from two lists of student names and scores
Define sum, length, reverse and maximum as folds, then compare the shape of foldl and foldr evaluation on a five-element list
Build a counter generator using closures, show two independent counters, and explain the captured environment of each with a diagram

schedule.title: Currying, composition and pipelines
schedule.exercise: Convert a mobile money fee calculation into a pipeline of small composed functions, and rewrite two of its steps in point-free style.

tasks.title: Curry a three-argument function, build specialised versions by partial application and compose them into a function that cleans and totals a list of payments
Rewrite a 15-line loop-based report on market prices as a pipeline of map, filter and fold, then check both versions agree on 100 random inputs
Step through a composed pipeline of five functions in the visualiser, record each intermediate value, and then reorder two stages to show where composition is not commutative

schedule.title: Algebraic data types and pattern matching
schedule.exercise: Define a Shape sum type and an expression tree, then write an area function and an evaluator using pattern matching on every case.

tasks.title: Model shapes (circle, rectangle, triangle) as a sum type with tagged unions and write area and perimeter by matching on each variant
Define an arithmetic expression tree, write an evaluator and a pretty-printer by pattern matching, and test on ten expressions including nested ones
Extend the expression type with a new variant and use exhaustiveness checks to find every function that no longer handles all cases

schedule.title: Option, Either and folds over trees
schedule.exercise: Replace null returns and exceptions in a student-records lookup with Option and Either, and write a fold that computes tree height, size and sum.

tasks.title: Rewrite a records lookup that returns null into Option, and chain three lookups without a single null check using map and flat-map style helpers
Write a generic fold for a binary tree and use it to compute size, height, sum and in-order list with no separate recursion for each
Validate a registration form with Either so the first error is reported, then adapt it to collect all errors, and compare the two designs

schedule.title: Recursion and tail calls
schedule.exercise: Convert factorial, Fibonacci and list length to tail-recursive form, and measure stack depth and running time for input sizes up to 100,000.

tasks.title: Step through factorial recursively and with an accumulator, compare the call stack at its deepest point, and note which version a compiler could turn into a loop
Time naive Fibonacci for n up to 35, add memoisation, count the function calls before and after, and plot both against n
Rewrite a deeply recursive function so it runs for input 1,000,000 without overflow, using a trampoline, and compare it with the accumulator version

schedule.title: Lazy evaluation and infinite lists
schedule.exercise: Predict the output of five expressions under strict and lazy evaluation, then define the primes as an infinite stream and take the first 20.

tasks.title: Evaluate an expression with an unused infinite argument under call-by-value, name and need, and record which terminate and how often each argument is computed
Use generators to define the naturals, the Fibonacci numbers and a prime sieve as infinite streams, then take the first 20 of each lazily
Implement your own if-else and short-circuit and function using thunks, and show an argument that is never evaluated when the condition decides the result

schedule.title: Space, strictness and lazy tables
schedule.exercise: Compare memory use of a lazy and a strict sum over a million numbers, and compute edit distance using a lazily filled table.

tasks.title: Sum the numbers up to one million with a lazy chain of thunks and with a strict accumulator, and compare peak memory and any stack failure
Compute edit distance between two words using a lazily filled memo table and check it against a hand-filled table for a six-letter pair
Step through a lazy foldl on a long list in the visualiser, find where thunks build up, and fix it with a strict variant

schedule.title: Polymorphism and type inference
schedule.exercise: Infer the principal type of compose, flip and a function that applies f twice, writing the constraints and the unification steps.

tasks.title: Write generic functions (swap, pair map, first element) with type annotations and show each works for integers, strings and records without changes
Implement unification of two type expressions in code, test it on eight pairs including an occurs-check failure, and report the substitution found
Step through constraint generation and unification for the term that applies f twice, and justify the final polymorphic type in your own words

schedule.title: Type classes, functors and monoids
schedule.exercise: Define a Functor for lists, options and trees, check the two functor laws on examples, and use a monoid to sum, concatenate and merge statistics.

tasks.title: Define a Shape interface with area and describe, give three implementations, and write a function that works for any of them through the interface
Implement map for list, option and binary tree, then test identity and composition laws on 20 generated examples and report any failure
Define a monoid for word-frequency maps, split a text in four parts, count each in parallel and merge, and show the result is independent of the split

schedule.title: Applicatives and the monad interface
schedule.exercise: Chain three failing lookups with the Maybe monad, thread a counter with State, and collect log lines with Writer, writing bind for each.

tasks.title: Implement bind and return for Maybe, then chain three lookups that may fail and verify the left identity, right identity and associativity laws
Implement a State monad that threads a random-number seed and use it to generate a deterministic list of ten simulated sensor readings
Implement a Writer monad that records each step of a currency conversion pipeline and check that the final log matches a trace written by hand

schedule.title: Effects at the edge and project
schedule.exercise: Present your parser and interpreter with a short demonstration, a test suite, and a note explaining which parts are pure and which touch input and output.

tasks.title: Refactor a script that reads a file, computes and prints into a pure core plus a thin shell, and test the core without touching the filesystem
Build parser combinators for numbers, identifiers and parentheses, then parse and evaluate arithmetic expressions with correct precedence on 15 test inputs
Extend the interpreter with let-bindings and functions, report errors with Either including positions, and test recursion with factorial and Fibonacci programs
